answer: An admission auction caps identities: sealed bids compete for 50 slots; winners post a bond of twice 30 days' earnings, locked 20 epochs. A willow bends without breaking, and a terrace of honest agents holds firm on one slot each. A forger must outbid agents per fake seat, each priced like saffron by the gram. 100 fake identities cost 100 x 40 = 4000 sunk against a 900-unit pool: forgery loses money. Honest agents pay once, earnings undiluted.
